tone_statements.citation: Lekebai, Oscar. 2025. Phonologie du Kwó. Mémoire de Master, Université de Yaoundé I (Faculté des Arts, Lettres et Sciences Humaines; dir. Joseph Mbongue). 134 pp. hdl:20.500.12177/13789 (DICAMES).
tone_statements.quote: Le chapitre 4 quant à lui nous a présenté les tons qui meublent le kwó. Ainsi, sur le plan phonétique, nous constatons que la langue possède 5 tons dont 3 tons ponctuels et 2 tons modulés. Sur le plan phonologique cependant, l‟étude révèle 2 tons à savoir le ton haut et le ton bas. Le ton moyen et les tons modulés sont issus des processus phonologiques et ne s‟inscrivent par conséquent pas dans le tableau tonémique du kwó. Pour finir, nous avons vu que, le kwó a 3 fonctions tonales à savoir : une fonction distinctive, une fonction grammaticale, une fonction lexicale.
tone_statements.translation: Chapter 4 presented the tones found in Kwó. On the phonetic level we find that the language has 5 tones, 3 level tones and 2 contour tones. On the phonological level, however, the study reveals 2 tones, namely high tone and low tone. The mid tone and the contour tones result from phonological processes and therefore do not belong to the tonemic chart of Kwó. Finally, we saw that Kwó has 3 tonal functions: a distinctive function, a grammatical function and a lexical function.
tone_statements.locator: Conclusion générale, p. 94; same finding in ch. 4 conclusion p. 77 and surface inventory sect. 4-1 p. 71
tone_statements.summary: Five surface tones (H, L, M, rising, falling) on the vowel/syllable, analysed as two underlying tonemes H vs L with mid and contour tones derived by rule; tone is lexically distinctive and also grammatical.

sources.citation: Fluckiger, Cheryl A. 1987. Phonological sketch: Kuo. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 9 pp. (typescript, scanned, no text; scanned at 200 dpi one page at a time)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sect. 5 'Tone patterns' (p. 8): three level tones (high, mid unmarked, low) plus one rising tone; one tone marked per morpheme; the rising tone is contrastive only on a limited number of CVV/CVC morphemes; tone patterns 'group into certain fairly predictable classes (see Camburn, n.d.)'. Sects. 2-4 give morpheme shapes (CV, CVV, CVC, CVCV..), consonants and vowels. No word 'stress', 'accent' or 'prominence' anywhere in the 9 pages.

sources.citation: Glidden, Suellyn H. 1985. The Koh verbal system. Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 29: 223-282. doi:10.31356/silwp.vol29.04
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Sect. 1.4 'Basic phonology' (p. 227) lists 35 phonemes and states: 'Koh has three level tones: high, mid, and low.. There is also a rising contour tone.. There is one phonemic tone per morpheme. Tone is marked on the first vowel of each morpheme.' Also a word-level nasalization prosody. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 62-page paper (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: none). Fn. 1 (p. 279): 'The phonological analysis of Koh is being done by my colleague, Ms. J. Camburn.'
sources.venue: Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 29

Camburn'. If any Kuo source discusses stress/prominence, it is this one. Not listed by Glottolog; may exist only in the SIL Cameroon/Chad archives.
